text: Some scientists argue. <break time="0.8s" /> That the universe is deterministic. <break time="0.8s" /> Because they can accurately predict the behaviour of many things. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as the orbits of the planets. <break time="0.8s" /> And have become better and better at doing so. <break time="0.8s" /> As various scientific breakthroughs have been made. <break time="0.8s" /> Science progresses. <break time="0.8s" /> And as it does so. <break time="0.8s" /> It increases our understanding. <break time="0.8s" /> There is only one direction of travel. <break time="0.8s" /> Ever better predictions. <break time="0.8s" /> For example. <break time="0.8s" /> 500 years ago. <break time="0.8s" /> We were poor at predicting many celestial events. <break time="0.8s" /> But today. <break time="0.8s" /> Using equations discovered by Isaac Newton and Albert Einstein. <break time="0.8s" /> Astronomers can very accurately predict. <break time="0.8s" /> The return of comets to our night skies. <break time="0.8s" /> Decades into the future. <break time="0.8s" /> The trajectories of spacecraft. <break time="0.8s" /> And the orbits of planets around our sun. <break time="0.8s" /> Similarly physicists can predict. <break time="0.8s" /> How magnetism will move objects. <break time="0.8s" /> And chemists can predict. <break time="0.8s" /> What will happen. <break time="0.8s" /> When some types of chemicals are mixed in beakers. <break time="0.8s" /> In ways that were unimaginable even a century or two ago. <break time="0.8s" /> Many bits of the natural world. <break time="0.8s" /> Are now predictable. <break time="0.8s" /> And that gives some scientists hope. <break time="0.8s" /> That the future of our universe. <break time="0.8s" /> Might be perfectly predictable.
